name: SanadSquad external editorial research seed index
disclaimer: Research leads and verified descriptions, NOT current production runtime evidence; re-fetch and validate every public claim before publishing

sources.title: Verifying Programs
supported_claims: Verified build matches deployed executable to source
Source equivalence does not imply security
Reverify after upgrades
excluded_claims: Verified means audited or secure
Upgrades are inherently unauthorized
relevant_customer_problems: Solana teams confusing matching bytecode with logic correctness

sources.title: Deploying Programs
supported_claims: Program authority controls updates
Authority can be transferred or revoked
ProgramData stores program executable code
excluded_claims: Retained authority automatically implies compromise
Multisig eliminates all governance risk
relevant_customer_problems: Protocol governance leads managing post-deployment admin privileges

sources.title: ERC-4626
supported_claims: ERC-4626 empty-vault share-price inflation attack
Mitigation design and slippage considerations
Vault share pricing and donation attacks
excluded_claims: All vaults exposed or mitigations absolute
relevant_customer_problems: DeFi vault developers facing share price manipulation and initial deposit griefing

sources.title: Proxy
supported_claims: Transparent and UUPS patterns have different upgrade controls
Proxy admin and implementation authorization require design review
Upgrade authorization behavior and privileged proxy administrators
excluded_claims: Upgradeable means insecure
OpenZeppelin audited SanadSquad
relevant_customer_problems: Protocol architects managing proxy upgrade privileges and storage collision risks

sources.title: OWASP API1:2023, Broken Object Level Authorization
supported_claims: An already authenticated user may reach another user's object when object-level authorization fails
BOLA is distinct from failed login authentication
excluded_claims: Every API is affected
Any specific unverified real dApp is vulnerable
relevant_customer_problems: Web3 application engineers assuming user authentication protects tenant resource boundaries

sources.title: OWASP API Security Top 10 2023
supported_claims: Differentiates API1 BOLA, API2 broken authentication, API5 broken function-level authorization, API7 SSRF
Function-level permissions and API trust boundaries
excluded_claims: A specific calldata/signing-front-end exploit unless separately evidenced
relevant_customer_problems: Security leads testing only login endpoints while missing object- and function-level authorization gaps

sources.title: MCP 2026-07-28 specification announcement
supported_claims: MCP specification revised auth hardening, request handling and routing architecture
Authorization changes address server/client trust boundaries
excluded_claims: Every deployed MCP server automatically adopts the updated spec or becomes secure
relevant_customer_problems: Infrastructure teams integrating AI protocol servers without defining clear RPC trust boundaries

sources.title: OWASP Agent Control Standard (ACS)
supported_claims: Agent transparency, runtime middleware hooks, inspectable execution and declarative policy enforcement across agent frameworks
Runtime execution boundaries to restrict unauthorized agent actions
excluded_claims: OWASP promises it prevents all prompt injection
OWASP specifies a mandatory wallet spending cap in dollars
Simon Willison is publisher of the OWASP standard
relevant_customer_problems: Autonomous agent platforms invoking external APIs and wallets without hard runtime boundaries

sources.title: OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications 2026
supported_claims: Reference framework for recognizing autonomous-agent security risks and building controls around tool-using workflows
excluded_claims: OWASP certifies a particular implementation as safe without independent evaluation
relevant_customer_problems: Teams deploying tool-augmented LLMs without formal threat modeling for autonomous delegation

sources.title: GitHub Code Scanning on Pull Requests
supported_claims: Pull-request security analysis can surface findings before merge
Workflow value of PR security checks
excluded_claims: GitHub endorses SanadSquad or its custom AI detectors
False efficacy percentages
relevant_customer_problems: Protocol development teams suffering regressions between periodic point-in-time audits

sources.title: x402 Foundation, Facilitator
supported_claims: x402 uses payment-required request/response signaling
A facilitator is optional but recommended for verifying and settling payments
Servers can handle verification and settlement directly
excluded_claims: Every x402 payment requires a third-party facilitator
HTTP 402 status alone transfers funds
relevant_customer_problems: Agent builders confusing HTTP payment signaling with required third-party settlement intermediaries

sources.title: MPP, EVM and x402 support
supported_claims: mppx supports MPP EVM charge and compatible x402 exact flows from one SDK interface
excluded_claims: Entire specifications are interchangeable or identically secure
All networks and payment methods are supported
relevant_customer_problems: Developers unsure how to design unified client interfaces supporting both x402 and MPP flows

sources.title: MPP, Improved sessions experience
supported_claims: A session can authorize spending once and incrementally extend authorization with usage
Useful for usage-based APIs
excluded_claims: Sessions eliminate authorization, replay, spending or settlement risk
All session costs universally decrease by the same amount
relevant_customer_problems: Autonomous agent applications incurring high overhead from per-request discrete authorizations

sources.title: NIST SP 800-218, Secure Software Development Framework v1.1
supported_claims: Security practices belong throughout the development lifecycle, including requirements, design choices, security reviews and software provenance
excluded_claims: NIST endorses or certifies SanadSquad
Following SSDF guarantees zero vulnerabilities
relevant_customer_problems: Protocol founders postponing security reviews until code freeze, discovering architectural flaws too late

sources.title: OpenZeppelin Proxy API
supported_claims: Upgrade-admin privileges, Transparent/UUPS architectural choices and authorization design create meaningful pre-implementation review questions
excluded_claims: Every architecture must be immutable or must use a specific vendor pattern
relevant_customer_problems: Founding teams needing architecture reviews before committing to upgrade patterns
